paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's door is open wider than anybody expected. Hezekiah's letter says, "the LORD your God is gracious and merciful; He will not turn His face away from you if you return to Him." (2 Chronicles 30:9) Some people mocked that invitation, but some humbled themselves and came, and that is the choice every baker gets too (2 Chronicles 30:10-11).

Now watch what happens at the table. Many people ate the Passover without being purified, "contrary to what was written," and Hezekiah prayed for everyone "who sets his heart on seeking God." (2 Chronicles 30:18-19) Then "the LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people." (2 Chronicles 30:20) Friend, I'm NOT saying the rules don't matter. I'm saying God looks at the heart that's reaching for Him, and He answers a prayer made for people who are coming back.

So what do you do with that? You come, you let Him clean out whatever's cluttering your house, and you keep your heart set on seeking Him. The joy that followed was so big that nothing like it had happened in Jerusalem "since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel." (2 Chronicles 30:26) Trust me, I know what it's like to think the invitation wasn't meant for you, and I'm still laughing about how wrong I was.
